tei:titleStmt.tei:title: שֶֽׂרַח בַּת־אָשֵׁר
Seraḥ bat Asher — a havdalah piyyuṭ by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer

tei:div.tei:head: Seraḥ bat Asher — a havdalah piyyuṭ by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer

tei:lg.tei:l: Seraḥ daughter of Asher, (×3)
speedily, between father and son, between mother and daughter she will reconcile.
The holy Torah mentions her twice!
Her name is found in the book of creation of earth and heaven;
listed in Pinḥas’ census for she went in the midst of the water.
Seraḥ daughter of Asher...
She came from the womb of the wife of her father, most blessed of sons.
She was righteous and all hidden things were revealed to her.
The sages interpreted that her life was long of years.
Seraḥ daughter of Asher...
She answered the pure one in wondrous tone that Joseph was in Egypt.
He rejoiced in her for she told him, “born to him on the knees
are your grandchildren, blessed of the Deity, Manasseh and Ephraim!
Seraḥ daughter of Asher...
The Bringer-Down-and-Up brought her down to the land of Ḥam,
to see where in the Nile the righteous one’s grave was delineated.
The years of enslavement ended, the time came for the people to be comforted.
Seraḥ daughter of Asher...
Right to the site she led him; it was raised from the reeds.
The armies of Pharaoh sunk and she passed through the Reed Sea.
She saw the stained-glass like the radiance of the Countenance.
Seraḥ daughter of Asher...
She merited to go up to the land from where she had previously descended,
and there to Abel-Beth-Maacah she turned her face;
she was wise in her city over all with understanding.
Seraḥ daughter of Asher...
They would speak, speaking back then, saying “Ask[foott]II Samuel 20:18[/foot] etc.”
So too, a time of stress came to her, for dwelling there in the mother city
was the son of Bikhri, an inimical and dangerous man.
Seraḥ daughter of Asher...
He had raised his hand against the king, and roused panic there.
The son of Ẓeruyah, in his rage, said to besiege with ramparts.
She said to him, “Why kill us?” He said, “Far be it!”
Seraḥ daughter of Asher...
Upright and wise are you; far be it from me to destroy!”
cried Joaḇ to she who is blessed and eternal.
“Strongly throw down the rebel’s head; this is what is necessary!”
Seraḥ daughter of Asher...
She rose and did this, saving the city in her wisdom.
By merit of all the wisdom of her mouth, another matter that she merited:
the abode of the Garden and paradise she saw in her life.
Seraḥ daughter of Asher...
The rabbis sat in the study hall to know how
the waters of the sea stood before Israel like a wall.
They learned, “like stained-glass,” for she was there!
Seraḥ daughter of Asher...
The wisest of wise women are you, and you will return in song;
you have aged four thousand years by the hand of the One who created you.
Rise, gather your people in Jerusalem the capital!
Seraḥ daughter of Asher...

tei:note.tei:p: Seraḥ is mentioned in Genesis 46:17 (Genesis being the book of creation) and Numbers 26:46 (in the census in the portion of Pinḥas). From this the rabbis determine that she lived through the exile of Egypt.

According to some midrashim (for instance, Sefer haYashar, Vayeshev 21; see also Ḥizkuni on Numbers 26:46, who cites a variant text of Targum Onkelos that we no longer have), Seraḥ was not directly the daughter of Asher, but rather the daughter of Asher’s wife who was adopted by him when she married into the family.

One of the oldest legends about Seraḥ, found already in the Targum Pseudo-Jonathan for Numbers 26:46. This stanza’s retelling is based on that of the Midrash HaGadol on Genesis 45:26, discussed by Prof. RabbiRachel Adelman in “Serach, Jacob’s Immortal Granddaughter” (at thetorah.com, 18 January 2024).
God, according to another well-known Biblical woman, Ḥannah, in I Samuel 2:6

Joseph’s coffin, according to sources such as the Talmud Bavli, Sotah 13a, was sunk into the Nile by the Egyptians. Seraḥ pointed this out to Moshe so that the Israelites could retrieve it and fulfill Josephs’ final request that his body be taken home.
According to the midrash Bereshit Rabbah 94:9, the wise woman of Abeh-Beth-Maacah mentioned in II Samuel 20 was Seraḥ.
Sheba son of Bichri, the rebel against David who fled to Abel-Beth-Maacah and who Joab was ordered to murder.
Find Derekh Eretz Zuta 1:18, where she is the ninth person listed who entered the Garden of Eden alive.
